meta.summary: trnrt serves one huge open model on one AWS Trainium2 box, and its checked equivalence claims and cost table teach more than its speed numbers.
meta.note: Backfilled on 2026-11-22: the run on this date could not reach the site. Picks, fit and verdicts are the run's own; stars, licence and last activity were read from GitHub on 2026-11-22.

picks.what: An open inference engine that serves one large open model on a single AWS Trainium2 machine through an OpenAI-compatible API.
picks.fitWhy: Serving on non-GPU silicon with a stated equivalence check and real cost figures; one model and one instance type only, so reading not adopting.
picks.caution: The serve container runs privileged with host networking. Benchmarks are the project's own, measured on an earlier build. Stars measure attention, not quality.

picks.what: A teaching-sized LLM inference engine in C++ and CUDA that rebuilds the core ideas of vLLM.
picks.fitWhy: Explains the mechanisms behind the serving settings I tune, in code small enough to read end to end.

picks.what: A fast renderer for Mermaid diagrams from the Obsidian team.
picks.area: Static-site and design tooling for an Astro site
picks.fitWhy: I draw many diagrams for my site and notes, so a faster Mermaid renderer that may run without a browser is worth a look.
picks.caution: GitHub reports no recognised licence (NOASSERTION). Read the licence file before any use.

picks.what: A layout engine for AI-drawn diagrams: the model names the boxes and links, the engine places them, in a hand-drawn style.
picks.area: Static-site and design tooling for an Astro site
picks.fitWhy: Splitting what to draw from where it goes matches how I keep layout rules in code rather than in prompts.
picks.caution: Ships as an installable agent tool. Treat it as code that needs a security review before use.

picks.what: An agent skill that tunes local LLM serving speed by trying one change at a time against a measured control.
picks.fitWhy: The control, candidate, control loop is a disciplined way to tune serving, but the repo is days old.
picks.caution: Installable skill: read SKILL.md and its scripts before running anything. Stars measure attention, not quality.

picks.what: An LLM inference engine built around a state-machine scheduler and a registry of kernels.
picks.fitWhy: The scheduler design is worth reading for how typed resource ownership could look in an orchestrator.
